title: Conformal flow and the Riemannian Penrose inequality with minimizing frontiers
main_claim: For n>=3, a complete asymptotically flat exterior with R>=0 (L^1, O(r^{-n-beta}) decay, h-delta=O_2(r^{-tau}), tau>(n-2)/2) whose full compact frontier is outer minimizing and locally perimeter minimizing (singular set of dim <= n-8, metric smooth through it) satisfies m_ADM >= (1/2)(H^{n-1}(Sigma)/omega)^{(n-2)/(n-1)}. For n<=7 this is Bray-Lee; the paper proves n>=8 by a Bray/Bi-Zhu conformal flow.

issues.description: The quantitative positive-mass step (small mass gives |Z-1|<eta outside l_n R) is not proved here. It is Lee's Theorem 1.3 run again with Lee's PMT inputs swapped for Lemma harmonic-pmt (Brendle-Wang), plus a stated correction to the scalar-curvature coefficient before Lee's Lemma 2.4. The adaptation is only sketched: the claim that Lee's constants do not depend on the interior is asserted, not re-derived. That claim is exactly what the limit argument uses, because the compact interiors change with t. This is a dependence that was not checked here, not a demonstrated error.
issues.evidence: "We apply the argument of [Lee, Theorem 1.3] at this scale... Both scalar-curvature coefficients ... must have this value... The constants in Lee's estimates depend only on dimension and the target error at the normalized radius, not on the compact interior."

issues.description: All positive-mass input for n>=8 comes from the external, recent Brendle-Wang Corollary 1.6 (no spin, strict R>0, all-order expansion), together with the paper's appendix on the weighted-minimizer singular-set estimate. The reduction from R>=0 on harmonically flat ends to that corollary is correct as written: the (1+tv) perturbation with -Delta v=rho gives R>0, and the mass changes by 2tA. The overall result is conditional on that external theorem.
issues.evidence: "We use the independently stated smooth positive mass result [BrendleWang2026, Corollary 1.6]... The smooth positive-mass theorem itself remains an independent input."

coverage: Read in full: introduction, geometry statements, flow.tex Sections 1-2 (setup, discrete flow, area loss, limiting minimum area, nesting, integral identity), mass-evolution, estimates, limit, completion, mass-capacity.tex (perturbation, one-sided smoothing, harmonic PMT, doubling/Miao repair), approximation.tex (cutoff plus Dirichlet conformal correction, main proof), and separation Sections 337-1086 (median separation proposition, graph equation, flow-slice separation, prescribed-curvature candidate, detachment corollary). Checked by hand: mass and capacity expansions (m=e^{-2t}m0+2e^{-t}B, c=e^{-t}(B+b), m'=-2mu); the integrated deficit identity and e^{2t}a=2e^t b-m0, giving mu'<=m-3mu and so mu->0; radius-bound constants (Hu<=2e^{-T}, K=4, gamma=2^{n-1}(eK)^q, cancellation of the time factors); the characteristic PDE for f_t and its integrated bound; the Kelvin-transform bound on j_t; the limiting radius r_inf=(M/2)^{1/d} as the minimizer of R^{k}(1+M/2R^d)^q, giving A<=omega(2M)^{k/d}; the B-J identity and its monopole bounds; doubled mass m-(1-a)c and the Miao corner sign (H_nu<=0); the discrete Euler lower bound and Bernoulli area-loss estimate; the flux identity giving A_R->m/2; and the Schwarzschild constant. Only skimmed: the simultaneous-regularity and relative-harmonic-derivative lemmas (separation lines 41-336), the geometry/proofs.tex enclosure proofs, the static hull lemma (flow.tex 156-505), and the weighted-minimizer appendix.
